text:
mira: Heads-up — running into a weird HF->Redwood chat_template conversion failure. system block in our Jinja template seems to disappear after conversion, and evals show a ~3% drop on our QA suite. Anyone seen this before?

kyle: Can you paste a minimal example of the template + the converted prompt?

mira: Sure. Original HF jinja chat_template (simplified):
```jinja
{% raw %}{% if system %}
- role: system
  content: "{{ system }}"
{% endif %}
- role: user
  content: "{{ user }}"
{% endraw %}
```
When we run hf2rw conversion, the resulting Redwood prompt looks like this (note: no system message):
```text
User: {{ user }}
```
No system section at all.

sophie: ouch. does the system variable evaluate to an empty string in some runs? jinja will drop the block if falsy.

mira: Not empty — we log it before conversion. It's present in the template render output, but the converter seems to strip any lines prefixed with "- role: system". Suspect a parsing step that normalizes roles.

dmitri: Could be tokenizer/special token interference? If the system content contains special tokens (e.g., custom sentinel or ASCII sequences), some cleaning step might treat it as control. Any examples of the system content?

mira: Example system content: "You are an assistant that answers concisely. DO NOT add disclaimers. <SYS_END>". We use <SYS_END> sentinel intentionally.

kyle: Try tokenizing the sentinel with the model tokenizer: `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('my-model'); print(t.encode('<SYS_END>'))"` — if tokenizer maps it to whitespace or drops it, downstream parsing might lose chunk markers.

mira: Ran that. tokenizer returns [101, 305], nothing weird. But conversion pipeline has a step that reconstructs roles by searching for well-formed role blocks and then joins content with `\n`. If the system block contains Jinja delimiters or unusual whitespace, the regex used upstream doesn't match.

eval-bot: eval-run: model-v2-int8 | dataset: internal-qa | metric: EM | baseline: 87.1 -> current: 84.0 | delta: -3.1 | suspects: system-prompt-missing

sophie: That explains the regression. Short-term workaround: 1) avoid inline sentinels in the system prompt; 2) ensure Jinja renders to a role block that the converter expects (explicitly include a stable marker). Eg modify template to always emit a system block, even if empty:
```jinja
- role: system
  content: "{{ system | default('') }}"
- role: user
  content: "{{ user }}"
```
Then in the converter treat empty system content as a no-op but preserve the block so parsing stays consistent.

dmitri: Long-term fix: update hf2rw parser to use structured parsing instead of brittle line regexes. If input is YAML-ish, use a YAML loader (safe_load) after rendering. That would preserve empty strings and avoid role dropping. Also add a unit test with jinja conditional / sentinels.

kyle: I can push a quick patch to treat `- role: system` as a hard anchor and capture the next `content:` lines until next `- role:`. Should be low-risk.

mira: Awesome. Also: adding a reproducible test case would help for the eval pipeline. I can add a small template + golden converted prompt and link it to the regression alert.

dmitri: Another gotcha: config.json tokenizer.special_tokens might need to include any custom sentinel (<SYS_END>) so that tokenizers don't split it unpredictably. Add it to the model card for onboarding.

sophie: Agreed. action items: @kyle patch parser, @mira add test + repro template, @dmitri update onboarding checklist to include sentinel in special_tokens, and @mira run a small eval after patch.

mira: Will do. Thanks all. :pray:

kyle: I'll open a PR and link the test in the description. ETA today. :+1:

eval-bot: noted: regression-alert assigned -> linked issue #4123

mira: If anyone hits similar weirdness, post the raw rendered template and the converted prompt — that'll speed triage.

sophie: nice debugging flow, thanks.
